Definition: from G575 and G4150; to rinse off:--wash.
BiblicalUsage: Once, on the shore of Gennesaret. The fishermen had gone out of their boats and were washing their nets — the word is the rinsing off of the night's work, the cleaning of the gear before the next cast.
TheologicalSignificance: A fisherman's chore, and the quiet before the miracle: the nets are washed, and then Jesus fills them.
